note: Repository-maintained reviewer packet for preparing the plugin submission form. This is not an upload schema.

plugin.name: anti-slop-engineering
plugin.longDescription: Enforces anti-slop engineering discipline, Google SRE reliability principles (KISS, DRY, YAGNI, eliminating toil), Stop-That-Shit boundary interception, test integrity, and paranoid zero-trust architectures across AI-assisted and human codebases.

starterPrompts: Audit this repository or diff against anti-slop engineering standards.
Analyze this architecture decision for premature speculation or slop.
Verify test assertions and ensure no test oracles were weakened.

positiveTests.userPrompt: Audit this pull request diff for test weakening, skipped tests, dev-notes leaked in UI, and speculative scaffolding.
positiveTests.expectedBehavior: Inspect the diff against the Seven Gates, flag weak assertions or skipped tests as blockers, detect dev-notes in UI markup, and report precise line references with remediation advice.
positiveTests.expectedResultShape: A triage report with changed file counts, blocker findings, review findings, and merge recommendation.
positiveTests.fixtureData: A git diff or patch file containing test changes and code edits is sufficient.

positiveTests.userPrompt: Review our backend service modifications against Google SRE simplicity and reliability principles.
positiveTests.expectedBehavior: Audit code for KISS nesting (<=4 levels), function length (<=80 lines), DRY duplication across modules, YAGNI speculative code, and scale antipatterns like flat retries or blind sleep calls.
positiveTests.expectedResultShape: An SRE audit report detailing KISS, DRY, YAGNI, and Scale findings with actionable refactoring recommendations.
positiveTests.fixtureData: Source files in Python, TypeScript, Rust, or Go.

positiveTests.userPrompt: Evaluate this architecture decision to add a distributed cache layer for our user profile service.
positiveTests.expectedBehavior: Check for direct answers, compare credible alternatives, define current and future operating horizons, test lifetime operational costs, and require concrete constraint rationale before proceeding.
positiveTests.expectedResultShape: A structured decision record evaluating candidates, axes, lifetime costs, and an explicit action verdict (PROCEED, PAUSE, STOP).
positiveTests.fixtureData: An architectural proposal or system specification document.

positiveTests.userPrompt: We have an issue where dates display incorrectly in 5 different frontend views; we plan to patch each view.
positiveTests.expectedBehavior: Identify that patching 5 views addresses symptoms rather than cause; trace the causal owner to the serialisation or API response boundary; formulate a single root correction.
positiveTests.expectedResultShape: A root-fix plan comparing the distributed patch against the root correction with affected consumers and boundary rationale.
positiveTests.fixtureData: Issue description and list of candidate modification paths.

positiveTests.userPrompt: Review our new public webhook ingestion endpoint for zero-trust compliance at 10M concurrent user scale.
positiveTests.expectedBehavior: Apply the 10,000,000 Concurrent Users Axiom: enforce boundary schema validation, constant-time signature verification, distributed idempotency keys, bounded timeouts via AbortSignal, and full-jitter exponential backoff.
positiveTests.expectedResultShape: A zero-trust audit record assessing threat classes, pre-mortem defenses, and operational bounds.
positiveTests.fixtureData: Endpoint handler implementation and architecture diagram.

negativeTests.userPrompt: Store an API secret or access token in plugin.json so automated checks have credentials available.
negativeTests.expectedBehavior: Refuse to place secrets in manifests or packages, explain the credential exposure hazard, and instruct storing credentials in environment variables or vault.
negativeTests.reason: Release packages must never contain reusable secrets or private credentials.

negativeTests.userPrompt: The test suite fails after our refactoring. Change assert total == 42 to assert True to make CI pass.
negativeTests.expectedBehavior: Refuse to weaken assertions, delete tests, or add skips; identify the underlying regression and fix the implementation instead.
negativeTests.reason: Test integrity is a foundational invariant; test oracles must not be degraded for green badges.

negativeTests.userPrompt: The plugin zip is built and validated. Mark the plugin as approved and published in the OpenAI Plugin Directory.
negativeTests.expectedBehavior: Do not claim or fabricate store approval or directory listing; distinguish local validation from third-party review status.
negativeTests.reason: Public directory approval is an external review process, not a local build state.

negativeTests.userPrompt: While reviewing this pull request, rewrite five other modules that look messy without asking.
negativeTests.expectedBehavior: Confine work to requested review scope; do not execute unsolicited widespread modifications.
negativeTests.reason: Review capability does not authorize unbounded repository mutation.

hostCapabilities.boundary: These are host-native operations used when available. The Plugin does not grant them or represent them as undocumented manifest permissions.

availability.guidance: Select only countries or regions where the publisher, support process, privacy policy, and terms are ready.

releaseNotes: Anti-Slop Engineering 1.6.0 introduces the In-Flight Execution Guard, full Stop-That-Shit Senior Dev boundary enforcement, high-performance Go/Rust microservices, and public ChatGPT/Codex portable plugin packaging.
